title: Count the content lines
prompt: Write a function named count_content_lines that takes lines, a list of strings standing for the lines of a text file, and returns how many of them still have text once the surrounding whitespace is stripped away. A line that is empty or holds only spaces or tabs does not count. The grader runs in a browser and has no filesystem, so the file content is handed to you as an argument instead of being opened with open. Return the count, do not print it.

title: Parse a config file
prompt: Write a function named parse_config that takes lines, a list of strings standing for the lines of a settings file, and returns a dictionary of the settings. Handle each line like this: strip the surrounding whitespace, then skip it if it is empty, if it starts with a # comment marker, or if it holds no = sign. Otherwise split it at the first = sign only, strip the whitespace off the key and off the value, skip the line if the key is now empty, and store the value under the key as a string. A later line with the same key replaces the earlier one. The grader runs in a browser and has no filesystem, so the file content is handed to you as an argument instead of being opened with open. Return the dictionary, do not print it.

title: Division that does not crash
prompt: Write a function named safe_divide that takes two numbers, a and b, and returns a divided by b. When b is 0 the division raises ZeroDivisionError, so catch it with try and except and return the string "undefined" instead. Return the value, do not print it.

title: Convert text to whole numbers
prompt: Write a function named to_ints that takes values, a list of strings, and a default number. It returns a new list holding the same number of items, where each string is turned into a whole number with int. When int raises ValueError because the text is not a whole number, put the default in that position instead. Return the list, do not print it.

title: Withdrawal with raised errors
prompt: Write a function named withdraw_result that takes a balance and an amount. Inside it, raise a ValueError with the message "Invalid amount" when the amount is 0 or less, and raise a ValueError with the message "Insufficient funds" when the amount is larger than the balance. Catch that ValueError in the same function and return its message as a string. When the withdrawal is allowed, return the balance left after taking the amount away. Return the value, do not print it.
